I need to make a decision in this Monopoly turn.

I have $1026 and am on INDIANA_AVENUE. I hold three houses on each pink property and one Get Out of Jail Free card. I notice a discrepancy: private notes from turn 98 show the pinks were fully built, but the current state shows only three houses each.

The game state is authoritative. I can build one more house on each pink to reach four houses total. This costs $300 and leaves me with $726. Four houses on the pinks is the maximum rent tier before hotels.

I'm reconsidering the hotel strategy. Building one more house on each pink would exhaust the three houses in the bank. Hotels require four houses, so I would need to sell buildings to fund them. I also need to verify whether standard rules allow a hotel while other properties still have four houses.

Hotels count as five houses under even-building rules. I can build one hotel on a pink property while the others remain at four, then catch up with the returned houses. I am now calculating the rent value of four houses versus a hotel to decide if the upgrade is worthwhile.

Standard Monopoly rent tables show three houses on St. Charles and States at $450 each, and Virginia at $500. The timeline event from turn 97 confirms p1 paid $450 on States Avenue, which validates the three-house rent for those two properties.

The rent increase from three to four houses on each pink is substantial: $450 to $625 for St. Charles and States, and $500 to $700 for Virginia. The opponent with the dark blue monopoly has only $2 in cash and cannot build further.

p3 is on Water Works with $77. They own the yellow set but have only one house on Marvin Gardens, and Pacific is mortgaged. Mortgaged properties still count toward a color group for monopolies, though no houses can be built while any property in that group is mortgaged.

p4 has $713 and four houses on each light blue property. They own Reading and B&O railroads and have mortgaged Electric and St. Louis. They just paid $450 rent on St. Charles Place.

I must keep Tennessee mortgaged. p4 needs it to complete the orange monopoly, and selling it would let them build there.

I am now weighing cash safety for my next roll from Indiana Avenue.

I mapped the spaces after Indiana Avenue. Rolling a 2 lands on B&O Railroad, which p4 owns with Reading. I noted the mortgaged properties and unowned spaces along the path.

Rolling a 2 on B&O Railroad costs $50. Atlantic Avenue has no houses and base rent is $22. Ventnor Avenue is $24. Water Works is mortgaged at $0. Marvin Gardens with one house pays $140.

Standard Marvin Gardens rent with one house is $120. The yellow set is incomplete because Pacific is mortgaged, so the opponent may not receive the full house-rent bonus. I am weighing whether to land on Marvin Gardens or take a safer path.

The house rent on Marvin Gardens with one house is roughly $120 to $140, which I can easily afford after building. I will not land on the light blue properties next roll from Indiana Avenue. Dark blue properties are also unreachable this turn because they require a roll of thirteen or higher.

I confirmed that p4's light blue properties are too far from Indiana Avenue to be landed on next turn. Building three houses to reach four on each pink is the clear choice, since the bank will be empty afterward. I considered building a hotel in a later action, but the available actions are limited to one tool call.

I will build one more house on each pink property now. A hotel requires four houses, so I cannot combine both upgrades in this single action. p4 is currently on St. Charles Place and will roll away next turn, meaning they will not land on the pinks again immediately.

p1 is on New York Avenue. From there, a normal roll lands on Free Parking, Kentucky, and Indiana before reaching the pinks. The opponent will not land on St. Charles, States, or Virginia from this position.

p3 is also safe from the pinks next turn. Their path from Water Works lands on Marvin Gardens, Jail, Pacific Avenue, and then moves past the pinks entirely. The only remaining danger is landing on Park Place or Boardwalk, which would bankrupt them. Building one more house on each pink is still the right move. Cash will stay at $726 after the upgrade, so I can afford any future roll.

Unmortgaging Tennessee or Pennsylvania Railroad would cost too much for the small rent increase. Trading Tennessee to p4 would complete their orange monopoly and let them build heavily on light blues. p1 has only $2 cash, so they cannot offer useful trades.

No trade can help me acquire red or yellow monopolies. The bank holds exactly three houses, so building one on each pink will exhaust them and deny p1 the houses needed to rebuild dark blues.

p4 already has four houses on each light blue property. They could build hotels there if they had cash, but they would need to return the houses first. I am checking whether taking all three houses from the bank would prevent them from upgrading.

Taking the three bank houses does not block p4 from building hotels, since hotels return four houses to the supply. The build plan is set: one house on St. Charles Place, one on States Avenue, and one on Virginia Avenue.

I will share my build plan publicly. p4 paid $450 at turn 101, which explains the cash jump from $276 to $1026 since turn 98.

The turn 98 thought claiming four houses on each pink was likely wrong; the first thought there only noted a two-to-three upgrade. After building to four houses, cash will be $726. The worst threats from Indiana Avenue are roughly $140 on Marvin Gardens or $50 on a railroad, and even a Boardwalk landing would cost about $300. A Chance card cannot land on Boardwalk from Indiana Avenue because Illinois is reached before it.
